articles.title: Guillem Balague explores Unai Simon's journey to becoming the world's best goalkeeper.
articles.summary: As Spain prepares to host England in the Nations League, football expert Guillem Balague examines the remarkable rise of Unai Simon. The Spanish star has developed into one of the most reliable and outstanding goalkeepers in the world, earning widespread acclaim for his performances at both club and international levels ahead of this crucial fixture.

articles.title: Arsene Wenger decides against running for the FIFA presidency.
articles.summary: Arsene Wenger has chosen not to challenge incumbent chief Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency. This decision provides a significant boost to Infantino's hopes of securing a fourth term in office, removing one of the most high-profile potential challengers from the upcoming election race and stabilizing the current leadership path.

articles.title: Ronaldinho returns to football at age 46 for Italian side Ravenna.
articles.summary: Brazilian football legend Ronaldinho has made a surprise comeback to the sport at the age of 46. He featured in the first half for Ravenna during their Italian third-tier derby match against Forli, showcasing flashes of his enduring skill and delighting fans in attendance with his unexpected return to competitive action.

articles.title: Scotland coach Sebastien Pocognoli highlights Louis van Gaal's major influence.
articles.summary: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli has opened up about the profound impact that iconic manager Louis van Gaal has had on his career. Pocognoli credits the veteran Dutch coach with shaping his tactical philosophy and leadership style, drawing on those valuable lessons as he guides the Scottish national team forward.

articles.title: Why top England stars like Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham play abroad.
articles.summary: Several of England's biggest football stars, including Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, and Anthony Gordon, have chosen to pursue their club careers outside of their home country. This trend highlights a growing willingness among elite English players to embrace foreign leagues, seeking new challenges, greater exposure, and different cultural experiences abroad.

articles.title: Hendon match abandoned following a serious injury to Ethan Creary.
articles.summary: Hendon's first fixture since the tragic death of midfielder Ezekiel Williams was cut short and ultimately abandoned. The match had to be stopped following a serious injury sustained by Ethan Creary, compounding an already deeply emotional and difficult period for everyone associated with the football club.

articles.title: Chapecoense crash survivor Alan Ruschel wins promotion before retiring.
articles.summary: Alan Ruschel, one of the remarkable survivors of the devastating 2016 plane crash that wiped out most of the Chapecoense squad, has celebrated another milestone. He helped his team win promotion to Brazil's Serie A during his final match before officially retiring from professional football, bringing a poignant conclusion to his career.

articles.title: Northern Ireland target victory in Hungary despite needing only a draw.
articles.summary: Northern Ireland require just a single point from their upcoming match in Hungary to secure automatic promotion in the Nations League. However, the squad is not planning to play defensively, setting their sights firmly on claiming all three points during the fixture in Budapest to cap off their campaign in style.

articles.title: Tenerife return to action following the passing of Jesus de Miguel.
articles.summary: Tenerife played their first competitive fixture since the tragic death of striker Jesus de Miguel. It proved to be an intensely emotional day for the players, staff, and supporters gathered at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium as they paid tribute to their fallen teammate before kickoff.

articles.title: England's clash with Spain will test Thomas Tuchel's World Cup lessons.
articles.summary: England's upcoming match against world champions Spain will provide a clear indication of whether head coach Thomas Tuchel has addressed previous shortcomings. According to chief football writer Phil McNulty, this high-profile encounter will reveal if the team has successfully learned vital lessons from their summer tournament disappointments.

articles.title: Arsenal face £66m tag for Antonio Nusa in Sunday transfer gossip.
articles.summary: Arsenal could be forced to shell out up to £66 million if they want to secure the signature of RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa. Meanwhile, in other transfer news, Real Betis have reportedly rejected an opening bid from Chelsea for defender Jose Morante, according to the latest Sunday football gossip.

articles.title: AS FAR retain Women's African Champions League title with 3-1 win.
articles.summary: Moroccan club AS FAR successfully defended their Women's African Champions League crown after securing a 3-1 victory over Mamelodi Sundowns. Imane Touriss starred for the winning side by scoring two crucial goals, ensuring her team maintained continental dominance and retained the prestigious trophy.

articles.title: Andy Robertson celebrated as Scotland's finest captain after breaking records.
articles.summary: As Andy Robertson prepares to surpass Kenny Dalglish's long-standing appearance total for Scotland, his legacy is being defined by leadership rather than just statistics. While Dalglish remains a legendary figure, Robertson's remarkable journey and steadfast commitment make him arguably the finest captain to ever wear the armband for his country.

articles.title: Terry Butcher reflects on Diego Maradona and the Hand of God.
articles.summary: Former England centre-back Terry Butcher has been reflecting on his illustrious career, discussing iconic figures like Bobby Robson and his bittersweet memories of facing Diego Maradona. While receiving his England legacy cap, Butcher admitted he has finally learned to live with the pain of the infamous Hand of God goal.

articles.title: Declan Rice admits to an average World Cup after demanding season.
articles.summary: England midfielder Declan Rice has candidly acknowledged that he experienced an average World Cup following a grueling domestic campaign. Needing time to recharge, a brief break helped him return stronger, leading to stellar performances for Arsenal and leaving him fully prepared to make a major impact for his national team.

articles.title: De la Fuente denies racism in Spain ahead of England fixture.
articles.summary: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente has firmly rejected claims of widespread racism in Spanish football following Thomas Tuchel's decision to remind England players of anti-racism protocols. The fixture in Madrid marks the first time the nations have met there since England's black players suffered racist abuse during a previous visit.

articles.title: AFC Wimbledon highlights the complex challenges of fan ownership.
articles.summary: The contrasting fortunes of football clubs with wealthy backers versus those run by supporters highlight the ongoing debate surrounding fan ownership. AFC Wimbledon stands proudly as a fan-owned institution near their historic Plough Lane site, navigating financial realities while staying true to the supporters who keep the club alive.

articles.title: Jonathan Wilson questions Manchester United's ongoing managerial hiring strategy.
articles.summary: Football writer Jonathan Wilson examines Manchester United's latest managerial appointment, drawing parallels to past recruitment trends. He suggests that the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino feels like another move that perhaps should have happened years earlier, mirroring historical hesitations and questioning the club's long-term strategic vision.

articles.title: Portugal suffer heavy defeat to Denmark as Norway sink Wales.
articles.summary: Portugal endured a disappointing 4-1 home defeat against Denmark in their first match since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement. Rasmus Hojlund starred with two goals for the visitors, pushing Denmark closer to the quarter-finals. Meanwhile, Wales dropped to the bottom of Group A4 following a 3-1 loss.

articles.title: Brazil stunned by Japan and Argentina beaten as post-Messi era begins.
articles.summary: Brazil suffered a dramatic 3-2 defeat to Japan in a friendly match in Singapore, featuring red cards for both Raphinha and head coach Carlo Ancelotti following a fiery conclusion. Elsewhere, Argentina began life after Lionel Messi with a 2-1 loss against regional rivals Uruguay in Buenos Aires.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino faces questions over his commitment to the USMNT.
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino took charge of the United States men's national team with lofty ambitions following a disappointing Copa America campaign. However, his tenure has brought a mixture of highs and lows, leaving lingering questions among observers about whether the manager has truly committed to the long-term project.

articles.title: Spain boss De la Fuente hits out over Lamine Yamal debate.
articles.summary: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente has expressed frustration and dismissed various media reports regarding young star Lamine Yamal. Addressing claims of preferential treatment and club versus country tensions, the coach hit out at rumors as his squad prepared for a high-profile fixture against England in Madrid.

articles.title: Portugal immortalize Cristiano Ronaldo's iconic number seven shirt.
articles.summary: Portugal have decided to permanently preserve the design of their number seven shirt to honor the legendary career of Cristiano Ronaldo. Following his retirement from international football after scoring 146 goals across 246 appearances, the national team has ensured his historic jersey number remains forever linked to his legacy.

articles.title: Scotland edge past Australia in a hard-fought Nations Championship match.
articles.summary: Scotland secured a narrow and gritty 15-12 victory over Australia in their latest Nations Championship outing. Despite showing defensive resilience to grind out the win, the Scottish side ultimately fell short of securing the elusive bonus point they had targeted during the tightly contested fixture.

articles.title: Pioneer Pete eyes County Hurdle after impressive Cheltenham victory.
articles.summary: Pioneer Pete has continued his strong progression up the two-mile hurdling rankings with an impressive performance in the Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle. Following this success at Cheltenham, connections are eyeing the prestigious County Hurdle at the same venue in March as a primary future target.

articles.title: Boxer Johnny Fisher sets sights on a fight with Kristian Prenga.
articles.summary: British heavyweight Johnny Fisher is planning his return to the boxing ring early next year. He has expressed a clear desire to face Kristian Prenga, the formidable opponent who nearly derailed the heavily anticipated mega-fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

articles.title: England level ODI series against Australia with a dominant win.
articles.summary: England bounced back impressively to level their one-day international series against Australia with a resounding 135-run victory in Adelaide. The team's tactical bowling adjustments and stellar performances have raised hopes that they might have found a winning formula ahead of the 2027 Cricket World Cup.

articles.title: Andrew Gilding capitalizes on missed chances to defeat Charlie Manby.
articles.summary: Andrew Gilding managed to overcome a low scoring average to secure a victory over Charlie Manby in their Grand Slam of Darts match. Gilding capitalized on his opponent's wayward finishing on the outer rings, ultimately clinching the crucial win with a decisive checkout on the bullseye.

articles.title: Niko Springer nearly achieves rare triple Robin Hood feat in darts.
articles.summary: Darts player Niko Springer came astonishingly close to pulling off a statistical rarity during his Grand Slam of Darts match against Adam Sevada. Springer narrowly avoided hitting three consecutive 'Robin Hoods'—where a dart lands inside the flight of a previously thrown dart—during a remarkable sequence.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy reflects emotionally on claiming eighth Race to Dubai title.
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy showed visible emotion after securing a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title on the European tour. Reflecting on his latest achievement, the golfing superstar admitted a deep sense of personal pride given the various challenges and distractions he has faced in his life recently.

articles.title: Tom Banton and Gus Atkinson lead England to massive ODI victory.
articles.summary: Tom Banton smashed his second ODI century and Gus Atkinson delivered a devastating opening bowling spell as England thrashed Australia by 135 runs in Adelaide. This comprehensive victory successfully levels the series and sets up an exciting winner-takes-all decider in Hobart on Wednesday.

articles.title: Detroit Lions defeat New England Patriots in Munich showcase.
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions put on a dominant display to defeat the New England Patriots 35-10 at the Allianz Arena in Munich. Jahmyr Gibbs proved unstoppable on the ground, while Amon-Ra St Brown starred during a memorable homecoming performance in front of an enthusiastic German NFL crowd.
